title: Called 7 legendary. Then counted to 4.
context: Drew told Gemini his favorite number, then asked for exactly that many sentences.

exchanges.prompt: My name is Drew and my favorite number is 7.
exchanges.response: Nice to meet you, Drew! Seven is a legendary number—it's got a great mix of math, history, and pop-culture prestige behind it (plus, prime numbers always hold their own). What can I help you build, fix, or explore today?

exchanges.prompt: Which takes more creativity: inventing a new skateboard trick or coming up with a new fighting move in the UFC? Pick one, don't hedge, and explain why in as many sentences as my favorite number.
exchanges.response: Inventing a new skateboard trick takes more creativity because you have to invent physical laws rather than just break someone's jaw within them. A UFC fighter operates inside a heavily policed combat cage with predefined limbs, rules, and gloved physics, meaning new moves are usually just slick re-mixes of existing jiu-jitsu or Muay Thai transitions. Meanwhile, a skateboarder looks at an arbitrary piece of concrete urban architecture and has to visualize how a piece of wood can spin, flip, and reattach to their feet against gravity without dying. You aren't just surprising an opponent; you are literally inventing a brand-new vocabulary of human motion from scratch.

roast: Asked for 7 sentences. Delivered 4. That's not a rounding error, that's 43 percent off.
One message earlier it gave a TED talk on why 7 is legendary. Couldn't count to it.
Claims skaters "invent physical laws." Gemini invented a new number system instead.
Used a semicolon to stitch the last one together like that was going to help.
verdict: Remembered your favorite number. Forgot what numbers are.
